newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends lower on stop-loss selling.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends lower on stop-loss selling.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures closed the TIFFE day session lower on Tuesday, due to late stop-loss selling after the yen's jump failed to boost the contract above a resistance point of 98.99.
The dollar dipped below 113 yen in late Tokyo trade, falling nearly three full yen from its New York close.
Traders said the market shrugged off an early report that the ruling Liberal Democratic Party will call for higher rates.
The December settled down 0.05 at 98.93 after moving between 98.92 and 98.99. Turnover was 67,785 contracts.
NHK television reported this morning that an LDP committee will make a recommendation to Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto by end-May that Japan raise its official discount rate.
An LDP source later said no decision had been made yet on whether to recommend a credit tightening. But the source said there were calls for an early rate rise within the LDP.
"There were similar calls from politicians for higher rates around the same time last year. So the market has learned to be calm on such news," said a city bank dealer.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) will raise its discount rate, now at a record low of 0.5 percent, only when it confirms the firmness of the economic recovery, he said.
The economy is on a gradual recovery trend despite the effects of the April 1 sales tax rise, the BOJ said in its monthly report released on Tuesday.
Although the tax rise brought about a drop in private consumption in April, the recovery trend for private consumption remained intact, it said.
In the Interest Rate Swap (IRS) market, some Japanese banks paid fixed interest rates for short-term maturities.

Those who received fixed interest rates from the banks sold the TIFFE Euroyen December contract for hedging purposes, traders said. The two-year IRS rate was quoted at 1.24/1.28 percent against Monday's 1.21/1.25 percent.

In the interbank market, key overnight call money was traded at around 0.51 percent, against Monday's 0.50. The open market benchmark three-month certificates of deposit were offered only at 0.57 percent, steady from the last issued rate.
The BOJ maintained a neutral credit stance for a third day in a row. It has done so since the start of the new bank reserve reporting period on May 16. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk
